To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the sampling rate of the sensor can increase up to one hour, while the interpolation and forecast accuracy is maintained; 2) the sampling rate and sensor wake up rate can increase up to two hours, while the interpolation accuracy is maintained; and 3) the sampling rate can increase to 24 hours, but the forecast accuracy is degraded.
we show that the sampling rate of the sensor can increase up to one hour, while still allowing interpolation and forecasting of future states with RMSE less than one degree.
the sampling rate of temperature measurements can be reduced by a factor of 12 while maintaining an accuracy of less than 0:2 C for interpolation and less than 1 C for forecasting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the time series of temperature measurements obtained from wireless sensor networks, in order to determine the optimal sampling rate.
the tradeoff between the energy consumption and data quality of a wireless sensor network.
reducing the energy consumption of a wireless sensor network by reducing the wake-up time of sensors and the sampling frequency of temperature sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accuracy of temperature estimation using interpolation and forecasting is not significantly reduced when the sampling frequency is reduced from every minute to every hour, while the sensor network energy consumption is reduced by a factor of 120.
the sampling period can be increased to one hour while maintaining the accuracy of the temperature measurements and forecasts.
the sampling period can be increased by a factor of 12 (to one hour) with no significant loss of accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of reducing sampling rate and sensor wake-up rate by 1 hour while still maintaining accuracy.
we have demonstrated that the sampling frequency for environmental monitoring sensors can be reduced by up to an order of magnitude while still maintaining acceptable accuracy.
the sampling period can be increased up 60 times without affecting accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of the sensor network is not significantly impacted by the reduction in sampling rate.
the sampling rate of a sensor can be reduced to one sample per hour without significantly affecting the accuracy of the time-series analysis.
it is possible to reduce the sampling rate of a temperature sensor network while still maintaining a good estimate of the temperature at intermediate times.
